answer: Mechanism: Echo-Karst Admissibility. Each agent sends nonces to random landmarks; admission requires return echoes over disjoint paths whose latency covariance matches a karst-like sparse topology (low-connectivity sinks) anchored to a rotating cedar backbone of long-lived relays. Sybil clusters produce dense internal echo loops but fail cross-landmark covariance. Cost: attackers must provision many geographically dispersed relays and sustain correct path latency/jitter across independent landmarks, not just spawn identities.
